name: Shillong
description: Capital city of Meghalaya and headquarters of East Khasi Hills, known as the Scotland of the East for its pine-covered hills, pleasant climate, and colonial charm.
facts: Named after U Lei Shillong deity

name: Shillong Peak
description: Highest peak in Meghalaya at about 1965 m, offering panoramic views of Shillong city, surrounding hills, and on clear days the plains of Bangladesh. Sacred to Khasi people.
facts: IAF radar station; ID required for entry

name: Elephant Falls
description: Multi-tiered waterfall on the outskirts of Shillong, originally called Ka Kshaid Lai Pateng Khohsiew (three-step waterfall). Surrounded by ferns and lush greenery.
facts: About 12 km from Shillong city center
Named after former elephant-shaped rock destroyed in 1897 earthquake

name: Ward's Lake
description: Man-made lake in the heart of Shillong, named after Sir William Ward. Popular for boating, walking paths, and flower gardens; locally known as Nan Polok.

name: Don Bosco Centre for Indigenous Cultures
description: Museum and research centre in Mawlai, Shillong, showcasing the cultures, artefacts, and lifestyles of indigenous peoples of Northeast India across multiple galleries.

name: Sohra (Cherrapunji)
description: Famous for extreme rainfall, spectacular waterfalls, limestone caves, and living root bridges. Sub-division in East Khasi Hills on the southern plateau edge.
facts: One of the wettest places on Earth
Gateway to Nohkalikai and root bridges

name: Nohkalikai Falls
description: Tallest plunge waterfall in India at about 340 m, near Sohra. Dramatic drop into a turquoise pool with cultural legend of Ka Likai.

name: Nohsngithiang Falls (Seven Sisters Falls)
description: Segmented waterfall near Sohra, dropping over 300 m in seven parts over limestone cliffs into misty forests. Spectacular in monsoon.

name: Mawsmai Cave
description: Easily accessible limestone cave near Sohra with stalactites, fossils, and short passages suitable for regular visitors.

name: Mawlynnong Village
description: Known as Asia's cleanest village, a small Khasi community near the Bangladesh border famous for cleanliness, living root bridges nearby, and community tourism.

name: Double Decker Living Root Bridge (Nongriat)
description: Unique two-tier living root bridge grown from Ficus elastica roots by Khasi people over centuries in Nongriat village. Requires trek of about 3500 steps from Tyrna.
facts: UNESCO tentative list related living root bridges

name: Laitlum Canyon
description: Dramatic viewpoint and canyon near Smit, offering sweeping views of deep gorges, rolling green hills, and misty valleys. Name means 'end of the slopes' in Khasi.

name: Mawphlang Sacred Forest
description: Protected sacred grove near Mawphlang village, preserved for centuries by Khasi tradition as abode of local deity. Rich in ancient trees, orchids, and monoliths; nothing may be removed.
facts: No removal of plants or items
